name: Leak protection
description: The adversary is trying to reduce or prevent any leaks from his systems to prevent leaving traces and de-anonymization.

subtechniques.name: Avoid carrying a cellphone
subtechniques.description: Phones can be tracked so to prevent this from happening, phones should be avoided completely or left at home or somewhere else.

subtechniques.name: Avoid commercial anti-malware software
subtechniques.description: Do not use commercial AV software that uses any ‘cloud protection’ or sends extensive telemetry and samples to their company.

subtechniques.name: Avoid devices with Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE)
subtechniques.description: These devices even broadcast information when offline and should therefore be avoided to prevent leaving any traces.

subtechniques.name: Avoid home Wi-Fi
subtechniques.description: Your home IP address is tied to your identity which could de-anonymize you. Public Wi-Fi or someone else’s Wi-Fi should therefore be used to prevent linking your activities to you.

subtechniques.name: Avoid leaving fingerprints
subtechniques.description: Leaving fingerprints could lead to de-anonymization. To prevent this precaution should be taken to prevent leaving fingerprints on for example packages or envelopes.

procedures.name: Confound DNA analysis
procedures.description: Accumulate dust from public places, containing the DNA of many people. Using toilet paper and wearing disposable gloves, lightly rub the dust into each component (cash, cover sheet and envelope).

subtechniques.name: Avoid license plate exposure
subtechniques.description: License plates are tied to identities. Exposing your license plate leaves a trail which might help to de-anonymize someone.

subtechniques.name: Avoid logging in non-anonymous accounts
subtechniques.description: Logging in to non-anonymous accounts could compromise one’s anonymity and should therefore be avoided en completely segmented from sensitive operations.

subtechniques.name: Avoid meeting people in real life unless neccessary
subtechniques.description: Communicating sensitive information to known organizations should not be done in person, unless there is no other option. Because this breaks one’s anonymity.

subtechniques.name: Avoid personal identifiable information (PII)
subtechniques.description: All personal identifiable information (PII) that you provide can be used against you and contribute to one’s de-anonymization. Never sharing PII in the first place could help to remain anonymous.

procedures.name: Privacy.com
procedures.description: Privacy.com is a supplier of virtual privacy cards which allow you to shield your card info. https://privacy.com/

subtechniques.name: Avoid photos which relate to you
subtechniques.description: Any photo which relates to you could reveal more information about you (metadata), your location, your friends or family, and so on. This information could help to de-anonymize you and should therefore be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid powering on burner phones at places that relate to you
subtechniques.description: The IMEI and IMSI can be traced back to you when used at the same location as other non-anonymous phones. This should therefore be avoided to break your anonymity.

subtechniques.name: Avoid printing invisible watermarks
subtechniques.description:
Many printers will print an invisible watermark allowing for identification of the printer. This could be traced back to you. Printing in color should therefore be avoided, because watermarks are not present without color toners/cartridges.

subtechniques.description: Public cloud storage providers will or must cooperate with law enforcement agencies and should therefore be avoided to prevent leaking any information which could trace back to you.

subtechniques.name: Avoid reselling harddrives
subtechniques.description: Avoid reselling harddrives because data could be recovered if not wiped appropriately.

subtechniques.name: Avoid revealing operational details
subtechniques.description: Revealing your operational details could be used against you and should therefore be avoided to remain anonymous.

subtechniques.name: Avoid sending physical materials via post
subtechniques.description: Beause of risk of leaving DNA/fingerprints, which could be used to de-anonymize you.

subtechniques.name: Avoid sensitive acitivities from untrusted powerline
subtechniques.description: It is possible to leak information via power lines, which could help de-anonymize you. Untrusted power lines should therefore be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid sign-up with famous services
subtechniques.description: Sign up with Google, Microsoft, Facebook, and so on could tie accounts together and reveal more information about you, such as IP addresses, timestamps, and so on. Which in turn could be used to de-anonymize you. Using this feature should therefore be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid SIM cards
subtechniques.description: Avoiding SIM cards wil block a phone’s baseband processor from communicating with cellular providers, which could be used to trace back activity to you and de-anonymize you.

subtechniques.name: Avoid Siri
subtechniques.description: Siri can record everything you say and should therefore be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid smart devices
subtechniques.description: The amount of devices with internet connections, such as smart devices, should be avoided because they could be abused and probably leak information.

subtechniques.name: Avoid social media
subtechniques.description: Social media are known for collecting many datapoints, which could be used to de-anonymize you.

subtechniques.name: Avoid the use of anonymous devices at home
subtechniques.description: Anonymous devices should only be used from anonymous networks, so home Wi-Fi networks should be avoided to prevent de-anonymization.

subtechniques.name: Avoid third-party software
subtechniques.description: Third party software might collect and sell information about you and should therefore be avoided whenever possible.

subtechniques.name: Avoid TOR gateways
subtechniques.description: Credentials and data are send plaintext over the internet till it reaches the Tor gateway, and should therefore be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid torrents over Tor
subtechniques.description: Torrent file-sharing applications have been observed to ignore proxy settings and make direct connections even when they are told to use Tor. Even if your torrent application connects only through Tor, you will often send out your real IP address in the tracker GET request, because that's how torrents work. Not only do you deanonymize your torrent traffic and your other simultaneous Tor web traffic this way, you also slow down the entire Tor network for everyone else. Don't enable or install browser plugins The Tor Browser will block browser plugins such as Flash, RealPlayer, Quicktime, and others: they can be manipulated into revealing your IP address. Similarly, we do not recommend installing additional addons or plugins into the Tor Browser, as these may bypass Tor or otherwise harm your anonymity and privacy.

subtechniques.name: Avoid tracking
subtechniques.description: Avoid software and services which track your activity, such as Google’s search engine or Microsoft Edge browser.

subtechniques.name: Avoid typing with open microphones
subtechniques.description: Recorded keyboard sounds might provide enough information to accurately reconstruct what was types. To prevent this, typing with open microphones should be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid unencrypted calls
subtechniques.description: Unencrypted calls can by eavesdropped/wiretapped and should therefore be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid unencrypted sites

subtechniques.name: Avoid using devices in front of a camera
subtechniques.description: Camera’s could be compromised and used to spy on someone. Avoiding the use of devices in front of a camera prevents this attack vector.

subtechniques.name: Avoid using real voice

subtechniques.name: Avoid using the same network for both decoy as hidden volume
subtechniques.description: To prevent leaving any traces which could be tied together, using the same public Wi-Fi network for the decoy and hidden OS should be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Avoid video/voice communication
subtechniques.description: When communicating sensitive information to known organizations, one cannot trust them to protect your anonymity. Voice and video communication should therefore be avoided to prevent de-anonymization.

subtechniques.name: Block trackers

procedures.name: DNSCrypt
procedures.description:
DNSCrypt is a protocol that authenticates communications between a DNS client and a DNS resolver. It prevents DNS spoofing. It uses cryptographic signatures to verify that responses originate from the chosen DNS resolver and haven't been tampered with.

It is an open specification, with free and open source reference implementations, and it is not affiliated with any company nor organization.

procedures.name: Spook
procedures.description:
https://github.com/EdenBlockVC/spook
This Ethereum RPC request mixer is a proof of concept that uses the Nym network to anonymize RPC requests.
This is useful if:
•You need to protect your real IP location of the entry node.
•You want to unblock yourself, if you're in a sanctioned country and you're using Metamask
•Your IP is not known by the exit node. Where you are in the world is not visible for anyone, it's hidden behind the Nym network.
•If the exit node is compromised, it does not reveal your IP address.
However, your exit node's IP address will be visible to the Ethereum node, but the entry node's IP address will be hidden behind the Nym network. Also, the exit node can censor your requests if it wants to.
You can use this as:
•RPC URL for Metamask or other wallets to anonymize your requests (prevent real IP logging, unblock sanctioned countries)
•local RPC URL for CLI utilities (like cast)
